title: Climate commitments/Paris and internationalised firms

source.request:
How internationalized firms respond to climate commitment??
Do they adjust their energi use, emisi, dan juga internationalization strategy-nya?
Do global climate commitments reach the factory floor? Did internationally engaged firms change their environmental behaviour more strongly after the Paris Agreement?

Outcome variables: 
VA/energy use, scope 1, scope 2, total
VA/emisi, scope 1, scope 2, total
Energi use, scope 1, 2, total
Emisi, scope 1, 2, total
GJ/emisi, scope 1, 2, total
Co2/va
Gj/va
Electricity
Self generation
source.strategy:
Matching per year: export vs non export, import vs non import, fdi vs non fdi 
DID


Apakah mungkin dengan staggered did??

Alternative: 
Freeze internationalisation status sebelum Paris, misalnya average 2013–14: pre exporters x year
2015 transition year
2016+post 
Firm FE + industry×year FE + province×year FE
Matching/entropy balancing dapat digunakan sebagai robustness untuk membuat pre-Paris groups comparable.
source.notes: Sesuai diskusi jumat (28 august), karena kita gak bs tau first time exporting/importing/fdi nya, kita bs coba dengan method matching yearly.. dan dicompare bagaimana behaviour mereka toward energy use, emisi, ataupun ekspor, impor, fdi…

question: Did internationally connected factories change their environmental performance more after Paris?
rationale: Separate changes after the common treaty date from the annual composition of exporters, importers and foreign-owned plants.
scope: Full exact Word row, interpreted through repository minimum checks and current owner full-plan ning/full-row acceptance gates. All analysis below is planned, not executed.
unit_of_analysis: Verified establishment-year for differential changes; supplied source-record-year for a separately labeled annual adjusted comparison.

target_estimands.name: Primary requested target
target_estimands.formula: q_it = alpha_i + lambda_j0,t + mu_p0,t + sum_{t != 2014} beta_t D_i 1[year=t] + epsilon_it; q in {ln(V/E), ln(V/C)}

symbols.i: a verified establishment, never a row-number or artificial linkage
symbols.V: value added deflated with a certified appropriate price index; any single-output-deflator approximation is named
symbols.Y: gross output deflated with its certified output-price index
symbols.E: scope-defined verified physical energy in GJ; incomplete observed subtotals are separately named
symbols.C: scope-defined verified CO2 in metric tonnes; not automatically all greenhouse gases
symbols.L: workers under an annually verified employment definition
symbols.X: predetermined measured covariates declared for the particular design
symbols.g: verified treatment-entry cohort in calendar years
symbols.S: a verified trade, ownership, industry, or survival state; unknown is retained as unknown
symbols.q: the named log real-value-added productivity outcome
symbols.lambda_j0,t: baseline-industry-by-year effect, only after classification certification
symbols.mu_p0,t: baseline-province-by-year effect, only after geography certification
symbols.D_i: participation group frozen from 2013–14 before Paris
symbols.beta_t: group difference in change relative to 2014

target_estimands.interpretation: beta_t is the difference in change since 2014 between groups defined before Paris. Annual standardized gaps are a different estimand.
target_estimands.limits: Paris occurred everywhere at a common time; exposure is selected, not randomly assigned. Shared export-demand and sector shocks can explain the contrast. No 2016 observation.

decisions.question: What does yearly matching estimate?
decisions.selected_rule: Annual IPWRA estimates the covariate-standardized ATE contrast in the prespecified trimmed-support population for that year. This is not ATO overlap weighting and does not identify a Paris effect. Publish the trimmed population and balance.
